A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices. Existing appendix content can be matched after the insertion of v3's new Appendix A.

before.justification: Sections 2.2 and 4 and Appendix A report original Colored-MNIST classification experiments and language-unlearning results using Phi-1.5 and Phi-3-small, including accuracies and Rouge-L scores.

after.justification: Sections 2.2 and 4 and Appendix B retain these original experiments, with numerical outcomes in Tables 1–5 and Figures 1–2.

M1.justification: The Transformer architecture, SGD and hinge-loss formulation, task-vector arithmetic, and low-rank and pruning constructions are unchanged. The new discussion introduces no method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Colored-MNIST classification and generalization scenarios and the same HP1, HP2, and Pride and Prejudice language tasks. The Phi-3 experiment in v3 Appendix B already appeared in v1 Appendix A.

E2.justification: The fine-tuned-model comparisons, merged-model configurations, and zero-coefficient baselines are retained. Newly cited He et al. and Zeng et al. works are discussed without being added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Model configurations, color-correlation settings, coefficient sweeps, accuracy and Rouge-L metrics, and the rank-32 LoRA experiment are unchanged. The relocated appendix experiment introduces no new evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The task-correlation and coefficient analyses in Figures 1–2 and the full-rank versus low-rank experiments in Tables 3–5 are retained. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary empirical analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version changes run-count or seed disclosures, uncertainty estimation, confidence intervals, or significance testing. The figures and tables retain the same statistical reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and Figures 1–2 retain identical results. For example, Table 2 reports 91.74% for the selected task-arithmetic configuration, and Table 5 reports an HP1 Rouge-L score of 0.1142 at lambda = -1 in both versions.

T1.justification: The definitions, theorem assumptions, theorems, corollaries, proofs, and multiclass extension are unchanged after matching appendix labels and relocated material. Appendix A discusses existing theoretical properties without adding or revising formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims concerning generalization guarantees for task arithmetic, task-correlation effects, and low-rank and sparse approximations.

C2.justification: New Appendix A explicitly discusses which task-vector properties are derived from SGD rather than separately assumed, highlighting bounded norms, near-orthogonality, and sparsity. This adds interpretation of the existing analysis while retaining its single-layer, single-head scope.

D1.justification: Implementation and experimental disclosures, including the model identities and LoRA rank, are unchanged. No hardware, training-time, preprocessing, or code/data-access information is added or revised.

R1.justification: v3 adds He et al. (2025) and Zeng et al. (2025), removes Jin et al. (2023), and replaces Jiang et al. with Cao et al. in the attribution preceding Definition 2. New Appendix A gives a focused comparison with Zeng et al., addressing chronology and assumed versus derived task-vector properties.

P1.justification: A short Additional Discussion appendix is inserted, existing Appendices A–E become B–F, and corresponding cross-references are updated. The main narrative otherwise remains essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: The new appendix causes limited reflow: Table 5 shifts downward and Table 6 moves from page 16 to page 17. Citation and URL text gains color. Figure content, table structures, and captions are retained.

improvement.justification: The new Appendix A and updated citations make the relationship to closely related theoretical work more explicit, particularly the distinction between assumed and training-derived task-vector properties. This provides a limited improvement in scholarly context while preserving the existing methods, proofs, and empirical evidence.
